To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

most neurons in the primate dorsolateral prefontal cortex with directional delay-period activity show sustained activity during a delay period in a delayed visually-guided saccade task, suggesting that these neurons are also active when sensory input remains.

most DLPFc neurons with directional delay-period activity show sustained activation when the sensory stimulus remained, and that the activity of DLPFC neurons during the delay period in a memory-guided saccade task was not unique to the mnemonic information.

most of the dorsolateral pre-frontal cortex neurons with directional delay-period activity are active when the sensory input is maintained, suggesting that the neurons driven by mnemonic input are also driven by the sensory input.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the properties of delay‐period neurons in the DLPCF and how they are related to the sensory and mnemonic inputs.
the properties of delay‐period activity of DLPFC neurons during memory‐ and visually guided saccades.
the neural mechanisms of flexible cognitive control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prefrontal neurons are involved in the working memory of the visual information and also in the working memory for the motor information.
the DLPFC is involved in the maintenance of visuospatial working memory.
DLPFC neuronal activity is driven by both mnemonic and sensory information, and that this activity is sustained in the absence of sensory input.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prefrontal cortex is a key brain structure that plays a crucial role in the flexible control of behaviour, which is essential for our daily life.
DLPFC is not a memory area per se, but an area that can represent information in a variety of ways, including memory and sensory input.
the DLPFC is not involved in the storage of sensory‐driven information, but rather in the selection of the appropriate action to be executed based on sensory information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prefrontal neurons that are thought to represent working memory are also driven by visual information.
most of DLPFC neurons active during the delay-period of memory-guided saccade (or delayed response) task are also active when sensory stimulus is present.

most DLPF neurons with directional delay-period activity are also active when sensory stimulus is present during the delay period, suggesting that DLF neurons driven by memory are also driven by visual input.
